html:
The Indus Valley Civilisation was a Bronze Age civilisation of cities along the Indus and its neighbouring rivers, in today's Pakistan and north west India. It is on the maps for 3000 and 2000 BCE, before and near the end of its mature phase from about 2600 to 1900 BCE. Its chart bar is Indus Valley (Harappan) civilisation.

Its cities, such as Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Dholavira and the port of Lothal, were laid out with straight streets, baked brick houses and covered drains. Bricks and weights were made to the same standard across a vast area. People wrote on small stamp seals in the Indus script, which no one has yet read.

Farmers grew wheat, barley and the world's earliest known cotton. Traders sailed to the Gulf, and Indus seals turn up in Mesopotamia. After about 1900 BCE the big cities emptied, perhaps as rivers shifted and rains weakened, and life moved to smaller villages further east. No palaces or great temples have been found, so how the cities were governed is still unknown.
